spec.name: Baku, the Dream-Eating Spirit
spec.description: A stylized ukiyo-e woodblock baku: a tapir-bodied spirit in indigo and cream with an elephant trunk, ivory tusks, tiger paws, an ox tail and a flame mane, shown in a neutral rig-ready rest pose.
spec.layout: Four-legged, facing +Z, standing on y=0 with all four paws flat. Tapir proportions pushed toward print-block stylization: a long barrel torso (z -0.85..0.65, belly y~0.52, back y~1.25), short thick legs, a thick neck rising into a big wedge head with a domed forehead (top y~1.45, ears to 1.58). A short prehensile trunk grows from the muzzle (z~1.2) and hangs forward-down to a tip near [0,0.72,1.62]. Short ivory tusks flank the trunk root, and long whiskers sweep back from the muzzle. A flame mane runs from the forehead crest down the neck and back to the rump, with flame wisps rising from the shoulders and haunches, an ox tail ending in a big flame tuft behind (z to -1.5), and a shimenawa rope collar with paper shide and a bell at the neck base. A dream-cloud scroll curls up from the trunk tip at the front-left. Ukiyo-e look on every part: flat colour only; bold sumi-ink outlines made as slightly larger sumi parts or thin sweeps behind or around key shapes (eyes, ears, tusks, paws, mane blades); indigo base with a cream saddle band over the mid-torso (tapir marking). Stylized pattern shapes are small parts in their own colours seated on the surface: seigaiha wave scallops (teal and white arcs) on the saddle, vermilion kumo (cloud scroll) roundels on shoulder and haunch, zigzag fur-edge tufts at the cuffs. Colour is warm vermilion and gold on top and accents, cool indigo below. Every colour is one flat colour per part. Detail comes from many small seated parts, not from smooth shading. Keep blocky, faceted, low-poly primitives.

parts.builds: The body shell: one loft (smooth-skinned over hips, spine1, chest) running from the rump (z -0.85, about 0.55 wide x 0.55 high, centre y 0.86) through a barrel mid-section (z 0 to 0.2, about 0.78 wide x 0.72 high, centre y 0.88) to the shoulders (z 0.5), then a thick neck tube over neck1 and neck2 (radius 0.24 tapering to 0.2) ending at headSocket where the head part's skull overlaps it. Coat colours by place: indigo back and flanks, indigoDeep underside and upper belly, a cream (paper) saddle band over the mid-torso (z about -0.3..0.2) wrapped by sectors, and a paperShadow belly. Print details as small seated parts: rows of seigaiha wave scallops (teal and waveWhite half-disc arcs, with sumi outline lines) on both sides of the saddle; vermilion kumo cloud-scroll roundels (disc plus spiral curl, with a sumi rim and gold dot) on each shoulder and haunch; thin sumi contour lines along the saddle edges and the belly line; small indigoLight highlight patches on the shoulders and back. Use b.surface plus stick, loop and along to seat all of it. Does NOT include legs, mane, tail or collar.
parts.attaches: Spine joints hips, spine1 and chest. The neck end meets the head at headSocket. Legs sprout at shoulderL/R and haunchL/R. Mane and tail sit on the spine line (spineLineStart to spineLineEnd, tailRoot).

parts.builds: The head, a faceted wedge with a domed forehead (skull from z 0.8 to 1.25, top y 1.45), bound to joint head. It has a separate upper muzzle (head joint) and lower jaw (jaw joint: cream chin, vermilion mouth interior, small ivory teeth). The face is settled first. Two big bold ukiyo-e eyes at eyeL/eyeR: a sumi almond outline, an eyeWhite sclera, a gold iris with a sumi pupil and a tiny white highlight, heavy sumi brow bars with vermilion brow tufts above. A vermilion tomoe (comma) in a gold ring on the forehead. Round ears on earL/earR joints: sumi outline disc, indigo body, paper rim, vermilion inner. Short curved ivory tusks at tuskRootL/R curving down and out, each with a sumi outline. Cream cheek ruffs of zigzag tufts. Four long whiskers per side swept back, thin sweeps in paper and sumi. The cream muzzle ring around trunkRoot. Indigo skull colour with indigoLight highlights on the brow ridge and a sumi nose-bridge line. Does NOT include the trunk tube, mane blades or collar.
parts.attaches: Skull overlaps the neck end at headSocket (z 0.92). Trunk root at trunkRoot [0,1.2,1.2]. The jaw hinges at jawHinge. The mane starts at foreheadCrest.

parts.builds: The prehensile trunk: a chain of four joints trunk1 to trunk4 with one smooth tapering sweep (radius about 0.1 at the root to 0.065 near the tip). It runs from trunkRoot forward and down to trunkTip. Indigo with cream wave-ring bands spaced along it (thin sweeps or discs: paper, with teal and sumi lines), a paper tip with two sumi nostril dots, and an indigoLight highlight line along the top. The trunk root has a gold collar ring. Also the dream cloud: a stylized floating kumo scroll of flat extrudes and discs in dreamPale and dreamPurple with sumi outlines, curling up from trunkTip at dreamCloudBase to the front-left (x 0.1-0.45, y 0.85-1.45, z 1.35-1.7). A moon-yellow crescent (extrude) and three small gold four-point stars float inside it, built from emissive-capable flat parts (glow the moon and stars). A thin vapour wisp (a sweep in dreamPale) joins the trunk tip to the cloud.
parts.attaches: Root joint trunk1 at trunkRoot, parented to head. The tip ends at trunkTip. The dream cloud's wisp starts at the trunk tip.

parts.builds: All four legs, short and thick, each a smooth sweep or limb chain. Front legs: shoulderFL/FR, elbow, wrist and paw tip joints. Hind legs: hipHL/HR, knee, hock and paw tip joints (hocks bent back, knees forward). Radius is about 0.14 at the root, tapering to 0.09 at the wrist or hock. Indigo leg colour, with the upper legs overlapping into the torso and the root radius burying into it. Cream fur cuffs at the wrists and hocks made of zigzag tuft blades (paper with sumi tips, gold stitch ring above). Tiger paws: a chunky rounded paw pad (indigoDeep with a sumi outline, bottom at y=0) with 4 toes (front) or 3 toes (hind) as rounded ivory bumps, each with a sumi toe line and a curved ivory claw. Small vermilion toe-bean pad on each paw. A thin sumi contour sweep down the front edge of each leg. Two small seigaiha scallops in teal and waveWhite on each thigh and forearm. Paw bottoms rest on y=0, with sole centres at pawFL/FR/HL/HR.
parts.attaches: Front legs root on chest at shoulderL/R, hind legs on hips at haunchL/R. Leg chains parent as in the joints list. Paws land on the floor at the paw mounts.

parts.builds: The signature flowing decorations. (1) The flame mane: a solid indigoDeep crest ridge plus about 40 broad overlapping extruded blade shapes (curved leaves with a sharp tip, a sumi-outline duplicate behind each of the larger ones) along the spine line from foreheadCrest to the rump, tallest on the neck and withers (0.25-0.3 m) and lower on the back. Root-to-tip palette: indigoDeep, indigo, teal, paper, vermilion tip, with gold accents. All blades lean backward like blown flame. (2) Flame wisps: 3-4 vermilion-and-gold flame extrudes rising and curling back from each shoulder and haunch (mounts shoulderL/R, haunchL/R), seated on the torso flanks, each with a sumi rim. (3) The ox tail on joints tail1 to tail4: a tapering sweep (indigo, radius 0.07 to 0.04) ending in a big tuft of about 14 broad flame blades fanning down and back at tailTuft (paper, vermilion, teal tips, sumi outlines). (4) A shimenawa collar at collarRing: a thick twisted straw-coloured rope loop (sweep, with spiral binding bands in a darker straw) around the neck base, 6 zigzag paper shide strips (shideWhite with sumi edges) hanging from it, vermilion tassels, and a brass bell with a sumi slot hanging at the front of the throat.
parts.attaches: Mane blades sit on the torso and neck along the spine joints (spineLineStart to spineLineEnd) and the head crest. The tail chain roots at tailRoot on hips. The collar wraps the neck at collarRing on neck1. Wisps sit on the shoulder and haunch mounts.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the design for a baku, a tapir-like dream-eating spirit, blending its traditional chimeric features—elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, tusks—with classic ukiyo-e aesthetics like indigo and vermilion tones, flat color fields, black outlines, and motifs like waves and clouds rendered in sumi ink style.

I'm now working out proportions and spatial layout: a stylized elongated body roughly 2.6 to 3.2 meters long with a curling trunk extending forward, a flame-like mane ridge along the neck and spine, and distinct sections for torso, tail, and head with jointed trunk segments, tusks, and ornamental cloud-scroll emblems on the shoulders and hips.

For the remaining structure I'm settling on five total parts: body, head, four tiger-pawed legs with clawed toes and flame-cuff fur, and a mane/tail/ornament group that includes flame-blade mane, ox-tuft tail, a shimenawa rope collar with paper shide and a bell, plus a small glowing dream-cloud wisp floating near the trunk tip.

Now I'm working out the part budget -- roughly torso 160, head 190, trunk plus dream wisp 130, legs 190, and mane/tail/regalia 200, totaling around 870 out of a 900 limit. I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy with hips as root, then spine, chest, and neck segments at specific coordinates, and defining the torso as a loft shape running along the z-axis with a narrower belly and wider back.

Still defining the joint chain...

Now I'm working out the leg joint chains—shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw for the front legs, and hip, knee, hock, paw for the hind legs—with paw centers sitting just above the floor plane, plus parenting shoulders to the chest and hips to the hip region before moving on to the tail.

I'm laying out the tail as a chain of four joints extending back and slightly down from the hips, then considering whether to add a separate mane role before deciding it's unnecessary since mane blades can ride the spine joints directly. I'm also planning the full joint naming scheme with left/right suffixes, tallying roughly 34 joints total across the hips, spine, head, ears, legs, and tail, and now moving on to defining the color palette.

Now I'm picking a ukiyo-e inspired palette: deep indigo blues for the main coat with lighter and darker variants, cream and shadowed paper tones, vermilion reds, ochre gold, sumi black outlines, plus accent colors like moss green, teal wave blue, sakura pink, ivory for tusks, and brass for bells.

I'm finishing out the palette with straw yellow, dream purples and pale lavenders, moon yellow, and eye colors in white and gold, landing around 21 total colors. For style, I'm planning to layer the sumi outlines as slightly larger duplicated shapes behind each part to create a dark outline shell effect.

Then I'm thinking through surface patterns -- seigaiha wave scallops in teal/white along the flanks, vermilion cloud-scroll emblems on the shoulders and hips, and flame-like mane blades gradienting from indigo to teal to vermilion at the tips. For color distribution, I'm mimicking the real tapir's dark front/rear with a cream saddle band through the middle, giving the baku indigo head and hindquarters with a light-blue seigaiha-patterned saddle across the torso.

Now I'm defining the skeletal mount points -- neck base, head socket, trunk root and tip, shoulders, hips, tail root, mane start running from neck to withers to rump, a shimenawa collar ring at the neck base, jaw hinge, and ears. Then I'm starting to lay out the bounding boxes for the torso and head geometry.

I'll add a tiny moon and stars glowing inside the cloud for the dream effect, then define the legs box touching the floor. For the regalia—mane, tail, collar, shimenawa, shide, bell, and shoulder flame scrolls—I'm setting a bounding box spanning the back and neck, with mane blades reaching up to the ear height and the tail trailing behind.

Now I'm working out the overall size and resolving overlaps between parts: deciding that the torso owns the coat, seigaiha pattern, saddle, belly, and the vermilion swirl emblems on shoulder and hip, while the legs own the leg tubes and sprout from joints that bury into the torso to avoid gaps.

Since the builders can't see each other's geometry directly, I'm making sure the leg root radius at the shoulder is slightly larger than the torso's surface at that point so it reads as a natural muscle bulge rather than a floating gap. I'm also sketching out the torso's loft stations from tail to neck, with the torso sweep extending up into the neck and head attachment point.

Now I'm designing the tapir head: a long wedge skull with sloped forehead and crest, exaggerated ukiyo-e style eyes with gold iris and sumi outline, bushy brows, round cream-rimmed indigo ears with vermilion inner, and short curved ivory tusks near the trunk base.

For the lower jaw I'm giving it a cream chin, small teeth, and red mouth interior, with the upper jaw forming the muzzle root for the trunk, plus sweeping catfish-style whisker tendrils in teal and cream. I'm also placing a vermilion tomoe mark with a gold rim on the forehead as the baku's dream-eating emblem, then starting the trunk as a four-joint chain tapering in radius with indigo coloring, a cream tip, and wave-pattern wrapping.

Now finishing the trunk with cream interval bands, small dark nostril holes, and a dream cloud at the tip. For the legs I'm settling on indigo limbs with cream sock cuffs featuring sumi zigzag fur tufts, cream paws with sumi toe lines, and ivory claws on tiger-style paws.

For regalia I'm deciding the mane runs as flame blades from the neck crest along the spine to the rump, colored root-to-tip in indigo, teal, paper, and vermilion, shaped like curling leaf scrolls. I'm dividing ownership so the torso carries flat coat patterns like the saddle, seigaiha, belly stripes, and shoulder/hip kumo discs, while the regalia covers the mane, tail, a shimenawa collar with shide paper strips and bell, and flame wisps at the shoulders.

Now I'm working out the tail design as an ox-like chain of four joints ending in a big flame-like tuft of vermilion and cream blades, also owned by regalia, and tallying up part budgets across torso, head, trunk, legs, and regalia to total 890. I'm starting to write out the joint hierarchy in JSON, beginning with the hips and spine chain and their positions and directions.

Continuing to define joints...

Still placing joints...

Continuing tail segments down to the tuft, making sure the hanging blades stay above the floor and the overall tail span fits within bounds. Then I need to finalize the floor contact points for the legs and nail the overall height with ears and mane reaching near the top, before writing out the full concise description of remaining parts and their joint lists.

I'm planning the trunk sweep function, using the existing trunk joints as the bone chain and building a catmull-rom path through their positions.

I'll taper the radius from the base toward the tip and shade it with color bands, adding a narrow indigoLight highlight sector along the top for visual depth.

Mapping which trunk bone each ring belongs to using arc-length positions along the catmull path, splitting the path into four joint segments with approximate knot values and choosing the nearest bone for each sample point.

For the rings themselves, I'm building a perpendicular basis at each path point from the tangent direction, placing 8 circular points around it, then sweeping a closed catmull curve with a small tube radius to form each segment.

Now I'm layering the ring bands: flanking sumi rings in thin dark strokes, a wider paper ring in the middle, and a teal accent ring sitting slightly proud of the surface, each scaled relative to the local sweep radius at that point along the path.

I'm interpolating a taper radius function across keyed values to shape the body, placing four bands plus a tip region, and adding two small sumi spheres as nostrils near the end cap, offset symmetrically and positioned along the tangent direction where the tube terminates in a rounded dome.

Adding gold collar ring details...

I'm planning the trunk's outline path with bones attached along the trunk chain, then placing the dream cloud bounding box and sketching a wisp curve rising from the trunk tip toward it using a catmull spline.

Now I'm considering the cloud's orientation and thickness—whether to extrude it facing forward or to the side so it reads properly from multiple viewing angles, plus adding small puffy accent shapes along the wisp.

Computing the cross product confirms the orientation faces front-left, so I'm placing the cloud box centered around x≈0.28, z≈1.52, fitting within the available width. I'm setting up a local coordinate helper that converts u/v/w offsets into world positions using the x-direction, vertical axis, and normal, then starting to compose the puffy cloud body itself.

Building disc layers for cloud puffs...

Since all puffs share the same thickness, the layering order doesn't matter and overlapping pale faces will always hide the thinner sumi rims beneath. Now I'm sketching out the coordinates for the cloud's puff cluster, placing base puffs along the bottom edge to build the characteristic flat-bottomed kumo scroll shape.

Adding a small spiral curl near the top, like a wisp or tendril, using a thicker sumi tube with a thinner dreamPurple tube layered just above it for depth.

For texture inside the cloud, I'm also considering small purple ring-like arcs on the fronts of the puffs, built as thin torus arcs oriented flat against the surface for subtle decorative detail.

Next I'm working on the moon crescent shape, building it as an outline combining two offset circles -- an outer boundary and a smaller inner circle shifted to carve out the crescent sliver.

Now I'm converting that intersection into the inner circle's own angle, getting roughly 64.9° relative to its center, and tracing how the two arcs connect: the outer arc sweeps from upper to lower intersection through the left side, then the inner arc needs to close the shape by going back from the lower intersection to the upper one along its own left side.

Working through the point arrays, I'm making sure the outer set includes both intersection endpoints while the inner set skips them to avoid duplicates, and marking the tip points as sharp corners rather than smoothed. Now I'm planning a slightly larger duplicate crescent behind the main one as a sumi-style outline effect.

For the stars, I'm setting up four-point extruded shapes alternating long and short radii for the outline, placed at three spots with their own darker outline copies behind them, then applying a glow effect to both the moon and stars using flat color materials. I'm positioning the moon slightly off-center so it sits properly within the cloud layer.

I'm working out the depth placement so the moon sits forward on the cloud's face with its own thickness and a slightly thicker dark outline behind it, computing the extrusion so it's centered correctly along the local axis. I'm also confirming the orientation so the crescent's opening faces the right direction when viewed from the front, and laying out coordinates for the three star positions.

I'm placing the stars near the cloud's puffs so they read as floating just above its surface rather than buried inside it, while nudging the moon's center slightly off so it overlaps nicely with the nearby star without clashing — though I need to double check how all this looks from the back view too.

Since the cloud back has nothing on it, I'll give the moon and star shapes enough extrusion thickness so they poke out slightly on both front and back faces, centering them so they protrude evenly. The outline for the crescent shape should sit at a slightly smaller thickness than the moon itself so the moon's face reads above the outline rim.

I'm also considering adding a few small decorative puffs along the cloud's wisp trail, using pale disc shapes with dark outlines, and tracing the wisp curve starting from near the top of the cloud dome rather than from the trunk.

Checking the cloud box dimensions fit the shifted centre, then sketching the wisp geometry with small rounded caps and puffs. I'm working out a helper to find joint positions along the path using tangent and closest-t lookups for the ring placement.

For the radius profile, I'm setting up a keyed array that interpolates smoothly along the sweep, with the trunk shape kept as a simple faceted circle rather than oval for now.

I'm figuring out how to render the wave-ring bands as a seigaiha-style pattern—pale rings with thin teal inner lines, faceted rather than smooth for the ukiyo-e look, and considering adding small scallop decorations between the bands on each side of the trunk.

Still placing scallop discs...

Since the tangent points mostly downward, I'll place the nostrils near the bottom-front of the dome tip, offset slightly outward on each side, and flatten the nostril spheres along the normal direction so they sit flush against the surface. I'm also adding a thin sumi outline ring near the paper boundary at the tip to define its edge.

Now I'm adding a wrinkle ring for paper shadow near the base, plus a gold collar ring circling the root with a slightly larger radius than the stick itself, accompanied by thin sumi rings bracketing it. I'm considering adding small gold studs spaced evenly around the collar using a ring helper to position octahedron shapes.

Actually, I realize the ring helper's item callback doesn't pass along the bone reference properly since the frame comes from a literal without an associated joint, so geometry would just snap to the nearest joint instead. I'd rather skip that helper and compute the stud points myself so I can explicitly assign the correct bone.

Writing trunk path code...

Writing ring helper function...

Tuning the ring radius formula...

Working through the radii so the teal ring sits visibly above the paper ring's crest instead of being buried inside it, I'm adjusting the lift value until the teal tube's top surface clears the paper tube's top surface by a safe margin.

Bands should stay visible near the trunk's bend at t~.5, with rings kept perpendicular to the tangent. I'm placing tip rings (sumi at 0.9, paper shadow wrinkle at 0.95), then designing a gold collar at t=0.05 with sumi rings flanking it and small octahedron studs in vermilion for contrast against the gold.

Now working out the collar's actual position near the root, checking how it interacts with the cream muzzle ring, and settling on t=0.07 with radius 0.1. For the scallop pattern, I'm stacking discs at the trunk's side points (t=0.3, 0.5, 0.69) in a seigaiha-style layered look—sumi outer disc, then alternating wave-white and teal rings shrinking inward.

Working out disc embedding...

Checking the cloud's bounding extents against the box limits, I find the x-range runs slightly too wide once puff offsets are included. I need to shrink the center x and tighten the puff u-range so everything stays within the 0.45 boundary.

Checking the y-range translates fine, and now I'm working out the spiral curl positioned at the top-right, making sure it stays within bounds while joining smoothly with the cloud's top puff, plus adding a thin connecting stem between them.

I'm offsetting the second spiral by a small normal shift and checking tube overlap — tightening the radius too fast over 1.25 turns causes the sumi tube to overlap itself, so I'm easing to 1.0 turn with a larger end radius and thinner tubes for both sumi and purple strokes. I'm also planning some puffs to get purple ring arcs via torus shapes on their front and back faces.

Adding purple shading discs...

Simplifying to one pale tube with rounded caps plus three sumi-outlined puffs for the wisp. I'm working out the tube's path points, making sure the tip starts inside the dome geometry and threads out through the front correctly near the dome's center and radius bounds.

I'm placing small puffs along the wisp path at varying positions with small, tapering radii near the cloud bottom. Then I'm setting glow strength differences between stars and moon, and sketching an eight-point star outline alternating long and short radii, extruded along the cloud's drawing plane.

Now I'm positioning the crescent moon and figuring out where each star should sit relative to the puffs, checking that star centers fall within puff radii so they read as nestled inside the clouds.

I'm setting up the extrude outline types to allow mixed sharp/smooth points, then writing a function to generate the crescent shape using arc parameters.

I'm verifying the intersection angle computes correctly and confirming the outer arc sweeps counterclockwise while the inner arc closes clockwise, forming a valid simple polygon. Now I'm considering scaling the whole crescent outline outward for a thicker outline, making sure the tips and inner hole scale consistently.

For the puffs, I'm dropping the cylinder's radial segments to 10 for a slightly blockier low-poly look, and confirming the orientation helper correctly aims along the given direction vector. I'm also weighing whether to add extra decorative touches like small accent dots or a shadow bar, but leaning toward keeping it simple, and tallying up the rough part count across trunk, rings, and tip segments to estimate complexity.

Tallying the remaining parts—collar studs, scallops, nostrils, wisp puffs, cloud puffs, arcs, spirals, moon, stars, and contours—brings the total to around 112, comfortably under my 150 budget. I'm now working out the highlight sweep sectors along the top and underside, confirming the rings sit just above the surface, then moving to write the hit-detection geometry along the trunk and the joint threshold logic.

Checking that each named joint has an `.at` method confirms the positioning approach works, so I'm finalizing the color palette references and writing the stick-geometry calls with embedded hit points tied to the trunk bones. For the nostrils, I'm computing a surface point near the dome's end by offsetting along the tangent and lateral axes, then using nearest-triangle lookup to snap a small sphere hit onto the correct spot.

I'm planning the buildTorsoCoat function, working out how to loft the body shape along the spine using stations with varying widths and heights tied to the hip, spine, and chest bones.

For the color sectors, I'm mapping angular bands around the torso to mimic natural fur coloring - a cream saddle band wrapped around the back, darker indigo belly patches, and transitional strips so the colors blend smoothly without gaps or overlaps at the seams.

Now I'm figuring out the neck geometry - whether to sweep across a chain of joints or build an explicit path connecting the neck base joints.

I should extend the torso toward the neck with tapering stations to blend the transition smoothly, narrowing width and height as z increases toward the shoulders, with the belly bottom resting around y 0.52.

Thinking through the loft setup, I'll use bone joints at hips, spine1, and chest for the path, assume the loft function accepts sweep options and faceted sections with elliptical cross-sections, and plan to use surface raycasting (skin.ray) to seat details like limbs onto the body at specific positions.

For the seigaiha pattern, I'm designing it as concentric stacked discs seated on ray-hit points: an outline disc, then alternating teal and white rings of decreasing radius and slightly increasing height to create a layered scallop effect, using a helper function that raycasts to find the surface hit point and null-checks before placing each disc.

I'm picking layer heights so the discs stack with slight overlap, then checking the curvature gap against the barrel radius to figure out how much the disc needs to sink below the surface to avoid visible edges. I'll handle this by translating the cylinder geometry downward instead of relying on the embed parameter.

Since true seigaiha scallops need overlapping fish-scale arcs rather than plain circles, I'm faking it with staggered rows of discs where lower rows get slightly taller heights so they visually overlay the ones above, avoiding z-fighting. I'm settling on roughly 3 rows by 5 columns per scallop section on each side of the saddle.

That's way over the 150-part budget, so I need to merge geometries per color group instead of instancing separate parts. I'll compute each hit frame's position and orientation, build a transformed disc geometry from it, and merge all same-colored discs into one mesh using the hit's quaternion and origin.

I'm now thinking about how to assign the merged mesh to the correct bone — grouping by nearest joint name like spine1, hips, or chest based on z-range, since skin weighting would look nicer but complicates the merge.

Triangle budget is tight, so I'm designing a Batch helper to group geometries by color and bone, then weighing cylinder segment counts to keep costs low — fewer radial segments and skipping unnecessary caps to fit within the 12000 triangle limit across up to 150 parts.

For the seigaiha pattern, I'm reconsidering the structure: instead of plain discs, layering concentric rings (sumi outline, teal, white, teal, white) to read visually as nested arcs, while checking whether five layers per scallop still fits the triangle budget.

Now I'm working out placement on the saddle flanks — three staggered rows along y with scallops spaced along z, offsetting alternate rows horizontally to get that classic overlapping wave arrangement.

For the overlapping discs within the scallop pattern, I need slight height offsets per row and column to avoid z-fighting where circles overlap, though interleaving multiple scallop regions with these offsets risks getting messy.

Actually, I realize I should shrink the radius instead to prevent excessive overlap between staggered rows — testing r=0.045 against the spacing gives enough gap to avoid overlap issues.

I notice the stacked discs will expose their sumi-colored sides like ink outlines where they rest at different depths, which actually looks appealing. I'll settle on r=0.045, ring step 0.0014, row offset 0.0075 with a sink of 0.008 to account for the surface curvature along the lower flank.

Actually that offset makes the relief too chunky, like a blocky carved puppet. Let me scale it back to row offset 0.004 and ring step 0.0008, keeping sink at 0.006 so rows 0-2 step up by 0.004 each, verifying spacing stays wide enough to avoid same-row overlap. Now I'm checking the saddle band's z-bounds and setting up a ray-casting approach from the x-axis to probe the surface.

For orienting each disc to the hit surface, I'm leaning on the SDK's aim function to build a quaternion from the hit normal, then composing the transform matrix from hit position, that orientation, and scale -- roll doesn't matter here since the discs are symmetric.

Now I'm working out roundel placement: using skin raycasts to get hit points and normals, then positioning the shoulder roundel around y 1.0, z 0.38, and the haunch roundel lower around z -0.55 to clear the saddle's back edge.

For the kumo spiral motif itself, I'm building small discs arranged along a spiral curve in the hit's tangent plane, varying radius from 0.045 down to 0.01 in cream paper tones, oriented using a quaternion that aligns to the surface normal so the curl lies flush against the body.

Working out the total triangle budget now: roughly 12 discs per roundel across 4 roundels, keeping segment counts low to stay around 1500 tris, and layering decal heights (sumi rim, vermilion, spiral, gold dot) with a slight sink so they read as inlaid rather than floating. I'm also planning thin sumi contour sweeps along the saddle edges near the body's waist to accent the form.

I need the sector boundaries to align with the actual loft path rather than estimated station positions, so I should compute them using the path's own closestT against the saddle points instead of guessing z-values.

For the sumi contour lines, I'm planning thin sweeps along the loop edges plus a belly line running along the surface at the midpoint angle, and possibly additional contour lines at the saddle edges around ±125 degrees to mark where the belly sectors transition.

Slicing the saddle line using closestT against the sampled body points, then mirroring the same approach for the -95 side. I'm also weighing whether to assign bone weights (hips, spine1, chest) to these line sweeps so they inherit sensible skinning.

For rings crossing the body, I decide it's simpler to skip explicit bone assignment and just let the loop carry its own blended weights, since picking a single joint per height gets messy. Now I'm thinking about small indigoLight highlight patches as flattened elliptical discs placed on the shoulders and back.

Computing patch orientation...

I'm placing the mane tufts along the spine line with small offsets, and adding shoulder patches. For the saddle border, I'm planning tiny triangular fur teeth using small cone geometries oriented flat against the surface via the basis normal.
